name: HPMA115S0 laser PM2.5/PM10 particle sensor
description: Honeywell laser-scattering particulate matter sensor with a built-in fan: reports PM2.5 and PM10 (0-1000 µg/m³, 1 µg/m³ steps) over a 9600-baud 3.3 V TTL UART, by itself in 32-byte frames (factory default) or on request. Needs 5 V ±0.2 V at under 80 mA (600 mA inrush). Sold as: Honeywell HPMA115S0-XXX standard-size sensor (43×36×23.7 mm) with an 8-pin Molex 51021-0800 1.25 mm cable (pins VOUT, VCC, N/A, N/A, RES, TX, RX, GND).
eli5: A small box with a fan that pulls air past a laser and tells you how much fine dust and smoke is in the air.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.description: 3.3 V OUTPUT from the sensor (100 mA max). Not a supply input: leave unconnected (pin 1).

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply input, 5 V ±0.2 V, under 80 mA running, 600 mA inrush (pin 2).

pins.name: NC3
pins.description: N/A in the datasheet: leave unconnected (pin 3).

pins.name: NC4
pins.description: N/A in the datasheet: leave unconnected (pin 4).

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Sensor UART TX output (0-3.3 V, 9600 baud): wire to the board's RX (pin 6).

pins.name: RX
pins.description: Sensor UART RX input (0-3.3 V): wire to the board's TX; needed for commands (pin 7).

buildNotes: Power VCC from 5 V (VIN/VBUS), never 3V3: the datasheet range is 5 V ±0.2 V; it draws under 80 mA running with up to 600 mA inrush, so add a 22 µF + 100 nF capacitor near the sensor if the 5 V rail is noisy.
The UART is 0-3.3 V, so TX/RX connect straight to an ESP32 or Pico: sensor TX -> board RX, sensor RX -> board TX. 9600 baud, 8N1.
VOUT (pin 1) is a 3.3 V OUTPUT, not an input. Pins 3, 4 and 5 stay unconnected.
The sensor's own connector is a 1.25 mm Molex 51021-0800; use a pre-crimped cable to reach a 2.54 mm header.
Factory default is auto-send: 42 4D 00 1C + 13 big-endian words (word 1 = PM2.5, word 2 = PM10) + 16-bit sum of bytes 0-29.
Commands are 68 LEN CMD [DATA] CS with CS = (65536 - sum) % 256; the sensor answers A5 A5 (ACK) or 96 96 (NACK).
Mount it in one of the datasheet's orientations and keep the inlet and fan outlet clear; stop() turns the fan off to extend life.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
from hpma115s0 import HPMA115S0

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RX}), rx=Pin({TX}))
sensor = HPMA115S0(uart)
while True:
    r = sensor.read()
    if r:
        print('PM2.5=%d PM10=%d' % r)

test.title: Reports the PM2.5 and PM10 set on the sliders
